issues.legal_issue: A technical error in identifying the secured creditor on a demand notice does not invalidate enforcement proceedings when the borrower understood who issued the notice and suffered no substantial prejudice.
material_facts: The lender advanced a loan under a facility agreement and took security over the borrowers’ properties; the borrowers later defaulted and their account was classified as a non-performing asset.
The demand notice referred to the facility agreement, the borrower’s default, and the lender’s claim, and used the common letterhead of two related companies with the same authorised signatory.
The signatory mistakenly placed the seal of the related company rather than the lending company on the notice.
The borrowers replied to the notice addressing the loan and their inability to comply, without raising confusion about the identity of the secured creditor or objecting to the seal.
The borrowers did not deny the loan, facility agreement, liability, or the enforcement procedure, and did not establish substantial prejudice from the error.
The Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal had set aside the Debt Recovery Tribunal’s decision invalidating the enforcement proceedings, but the High Court reversed that decision in a writ petition.
issues.conclusion: The seal error was a trivial technical defect that did not invalidate the enforcement proceedings; the appeal was allowed and the High Court’s judgment was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 13(2), 13(3A), 13(4), 14 and 17 of the SARFAESI Act, a procedural lapse does not by itself invalidate enforcement where the affected person knew who was taking action and cannot show substantial prejudice. Whether a lapse is material depends on the facts of each case; there is no uniform formula. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: sarfaesi_enforcement_proceeding and notice_identifies_underlying_debt and creditor_identity_understood and technical_identification_error and no_substantial_prejudice

predicates.sarfaesi_enforcement_proceeding: A secured creditor initiated statutory enforcement proceedings against a borrower after default on a secured loan.
predicates.notice_identifies_underlying_debt: The notice connected the demand to the parties’ loan agreement and the borrower’s default.
predicates.creditor_identity_understood: The borrower’s response showed that the borrower understood which secured creditor was demanding repayment.
predicates.technical_identification_error: The notice contained a mistaken company seal or similar technical error despite being issued in the context of the creditor’s dealings with the borrower.
predicates.no_substantial_prejudice: The borrower did not show that the procedural error caused substantial prejudice.

issues.definition: When a secured creditor pursues enforcement, the notice identifies the underlying debt, the borrower understands the creditor’s identity, the identification error is technical, and the borrower suffers no substantial prejudice, the enforcement proceedings are not invalidated.
